sub: For travellers from the US, UK, Europe, Australia and Canada going to India on their own: where to start, how to move between cities alone, what your government's advice says, and how a private car and driver fits a solo trip.

answer: Yes — many people travel India alone. Start on a well-trodden route (Delhi, Agra, Jaipur, then Rishikesh or the Himalayan foothills), book your first night and airport transfer before you land, move by train, flight or a private car with driver, and carry a local SIM. Save 112 and the tourist helpline 1363, and read your government's advice first. Solo prices are on request.

sections.h2: How to get around India alone
sections.lead: Three ways to move between cities, plus the short hops in between. Many solo travellers mix them. Our trains vs flights guide compares the first two in detail.
items: Trains

You can book IRCTC's Foreign Tourist quota yourself with a foreign passport — up to 365 days ahead, paying by international card. Carry your original passport on board. Travel agents cannot book that quota for you.
Flights
For long distances — Delhi to Goa, Kerala or Ladakh — a domestic flight saves a day of travel. Book directly with the airline.
A private car and driver

Your own car and English-speaking driver from city to city: door to door, stops when you want them, and one place for your luggage. Your driver's name, photo and car number are shared with you before the trip. See private car with driver.
Taxis in town

The UK FCDO says app-based taxis like Uber and Ola are widely available, including in all airport terminal buildings, and that pre-paid taxis and hotel transfers are also available. It advises: “Avoid travelling alone and hailing taxis on the street, especially at night.”
Arriving
Australia's Smartraveller says: “Use a pre-paid taxi service when you arrive at the airport.” Easiest of all on a first trip: book your first night's hotel with an airport transfer before you fly.

sections.h2: What to sort out before you land
items: Your visa — on the official site only

Apply only at the official site indianvisaonline.gov.in — beware look-alike sites that charge extra. We are not a visa agency. In November 2026 the Government of India announced that the Tourist Visa is being renamed the Visitor Visa (PIB, 11 Nov 2026); until the official site changes, apply for the visa it shows there. Our e-Visa guide walks through it.
Travel insurance
Alone, there is no one else to pay a hospital bill or rebook a flight — read our India travel insurance guide.
A local SIM or eSIM
Maps, app taxis and staying in touch all depend on data. Our SIM card guide explains the options for foreigners.
Money
Plan on cards and some cash as your main way to pay. UPI for foreign visitors is still a pilot — check NPCI before you rely on it. See UPI and money in India.
Your health
We're a travel company, not doctors: consult your doctor or a travel clinic, and see CDC or NHS Fit for Travel.
Your first night
Book your first hotel and airport transfer in advance, and share your plan with someone at home.

sections.h2: Is it safe to travel India alone? What the governments say
sections.text: Read your own government's advice before you book — this is a short summary, not a promise. The US State Department rates India Level 2: “Exercise increased caution in India due to crime and terrorism. Some areas have increased risk.” (issued 16 Jun 2025). Its country page adds: “The U.S. government advises against women traveling alone in India.” The UK FCDO (advice checked 19 Nov 2026) says: “Avoid travelling alone and hailing taxis on the street, especially at night” and “Be wary of accepting drinks or food from strangers or leaving drinks unattended.” Australia's Smartraveller asks you to “exercise a high degree of caution in India overall” and “don't hail taxis on the street.” Travelling alone as a woman? Read our dedicated guide: Is India safe for solo female travellers? Staying at an ashram or retreat? Choose retreats and hosts carefully and read recent independent reviews — Australia's Smartraveller warns of misconduct allegations involving some religious groups.

faqs: Is India good for a first solo trip?

Yes, if you start on the main tourist circuit — Delhi, Agra and Jaipur — where transport and hotels are easiest, then slow down in Rishikesh or the Himalayan foothills. Book your first night and airport transfer before you land.
Is it safe to travel India alone?

Read your own government's advice first. The US State Department rates India Level 2 (exercise increased caution, issued 16 Jun 2025); the UK FCDO advises avoiding travelling alone and hailing taxis on the street, especially at night. Women travelling alone should read our dedicated guide, Is India safe for solo female travellers?
Where should I go on my first solo trip to India?

Delhi, Agra (the Taj Mahal) and Jaipur for a week; add Rishikesh and McLeod Ganj in the Himalayan foothills for two weeks. All are on the main tourist circuit, so trains, cars and hotels are easy to arrange.
How do I get around India alone?

Trains (book IRCTC's Foreign Tourist quota yourself with your passport, up to 365 days ahead), domestic flights for long distances, or a private car with driver. In cities, the UK FCDO says app taxis like Uber and Ola are widely available.
Can I hire a private car and driver just for myself?
Yes — a private car with an English-speaking driver works for one traveller just as for a group. Your driver's name, photo and car number are shared with you before the trip. Ask us for a solo quote.
What phone numbers should I save in India?
112 for emergencies, 100 for police, 1091 for the women's helpline, and the Ministry of Tourism's 24×7 multilingual tourist helpline 1800-11-1363 (short code 1363). Also save your embassy's number.
Should I join a group tour or travel alone?

Both work. A group gives company and a fixed plan; going fully independent gives total freedom and more planning. A private car and driver sits in between: your own route and pace, with someone local on call.
How much does a solo trip to India cost?

It depends on your route, hotel level, how you travel and the season. Our hub routes start from US$299 per person; for one traveller we quote the private car and a single room separately — ask for a solo quote.
